correctness.rationale: For all n>=1, direct local edge-state analysis equates excitation events to increments of closed-neighborhood maxima of an integer height. At time n-1 the last possible new excitation is precisely a strict height record at one endpoint, and the two endpoint events are disjoint. The positive-height reversed-word transfer with a killed boundary yields a unique formal-series kernel solution S(z)=(sqrt((1+z)/(1-3z))-1)/(2z), hence the claimed maximal-entry census and exact n^-1/2 asymptotic. The n=1 edge case is treated separately. Full original-state tests n<=12, independent transfer n<=101 and gradient/maxplus tests n<=8 passed. These finite checks do not replace the general derivation.

value.rationale: Exact counts at the sharp extinction-time boundary are a natural infinite-family invariant for dissipative excitable dynamics. The polynomial 1/sqrt(n) extremal-tail probability distinguishes a geometric boundary-wave phenomenon from generic extinction and remains mathematically motivated despite the already-known integer sequence. The object, quantifier and probabilistic observable are not arbitrarily chosen, and no broader theorem is required for this exact natural boundary classification.
